question.text: An offshore Cayman master fund wants to appoint Mr. Vikram Shah, India-based, as its fund manager without triggering a 'business connection' / POEM risk for the offshore fund. Which ITA provision offers a safe harbour, and which is a KEY condition?

answer.text: Section 115UB — India-resident sponsor must hold < 20% units

Section 9A — among other conditions: the eligible investment fund must have at least 25 members, India-resident investors' aggregate participation must not exceed 5%, and the fund manager must be remunerated at arm's length

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Section 9A of the ITA (Eligible Investment Fund + Eligible Fund Manager safe harbour) lets an India-based fund manager advise an offshore fund without the activity being deemed to create a business connection in India for the offshore fund. Conditions include minimum 25 members (no concentration), maximum 5% participation by India residents, arm's-length remuneration to the manager, and the fund not carrying on business in India other than investment activity. **The Trap:** Option A is the Cat I/II pass-through section — unrelated. Option C is the beneficial-treaty rule. Option D is business-trust (REIT/InvIT) distribution TDS. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-A doesn't cover Section 9A; XIX-C expects the manager to know the GIFT-City IFSC alternative to Section 9A (Fund Management (IFSCA) Regulations 2022 also expressly covered by the 115UB definition of 'Investment Fund'). **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Compare Section 9A onshore vs IFSC GIFT-City structuring before advising a global sponsor. GIFT offers tax holidays plus the Fund Management Regulations 2022; 9A has 12+ conditions that many funds fail. Many large managers today run a GIFT feeder.
